title.zh: 卷七十 列傳第三十 袁淑
title.raw: 卷七十 列傳第三十 袁淑 Volume 70 Biographies 30: Yuan Shu

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十 袁淑

translations.literal: Biography 30: Yuan Shu
translations.idiomatic: Biography 30: Yuan Shu

sentences.zh: 袁淑，字陽源，陳郡陽夏人，丹陽尹豹少子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, the youngest son of Bao, Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery; he was the youngest son of Bao, Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少有風氣，年數歲，伯湛謂家人曰：「此非凡兒。

translations.literal: From youth he had spirit and bearing; when only a few years old, his uncle Zhan said to the family: “This is no ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed unusual presence; when he was only a few years old, his uncle Zhan told the household, “This is no ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 」至十餘歲，為姑夫王弘所賞。

translations.literal: ” By his teens he was admired by his brother-in-law Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: ” In his mid-teens he won the esteem of his brother-in-law Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 不為章句之學，而博涉多通，好屬文，辭采遒豔，縱橫有才辯。

translations.literal: He did not pursue the study of chapter-and-sentence exegesis, but ranged widely and mastered many fields; he loved literary composition, and his style was forceful and brilliant, with talent for sweeping eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: He did not train in formal philological commentary, yet he read broadly and knew many subjects; he delighted in writing, his prose vivid and vigorous, and he was a bold, gifted debater.

sentences.zh: 本州命主簿，著作佐郎，太子舍人，並不就。

translations.literal: The province appointed him chief clerk; he was offered posts as Editorial Assistant and Crown Prince’s Attendant — he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration named him chief clerk, and he was offered the posts of Editorial Assistant and Crown Prince’s Attendant, but he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康命為軍司祭酒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Liu Yikang, appointed him Libationer of the Army Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, made him Libationer of the Army Staff.

sentences.zh: 義康不好文學，雖外相禮接，意好甚疏。

translations.literal: Yikang did not care for literature; though outwardly courteous in receiving him, his regard was very thin.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang had little taste for letters; though he treated Shu with outward courtesy, his affection was remote.

sentences.zh: 劉湛，淑從母兄也，欲其附己，而淑不以為意，由是大相乖失，以久疾免官。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan was Shu’s maternal cousin and wished Shu to attach himself to him, but Shu paid no heed; they therefore became greatly estranged, and Shu was dismissed from office after a long illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, Shu’s cousin on his mother’s side, wanted Shu to side with him, but Shu took no notice; the two fell sharply apart, and Shu was eventually relieved of office after a prolonged illness.

sentences.zh: 補衡陽王義季右軍主簿，遷太子洗馬，以腳疾不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk to the Right Army of the Prince of Hengyang, Liu Yiji, then promoted to Crown Prince’s Groom, but did not take office because of a foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Chief Clerk to the Right Army of Liu Yiji, Prince of Hengyang, then promoted to Crown Prince’s Groom, but declined the appointment on account of lameness.

sentences.zh: 衛軍臨川王義慶雅好文章，請為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: The Defender-in-Chief, the Prince of Linchuan Liu Yiqing, who dearly loved literature, invited him to serve as Consulting Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan and Defender-in-Chief, who greatly loved literary work, asked him to serve as Consulting Commander.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Western Attendant of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was moved to Left Western Attendant under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為宣城太守，入補中書侍郎，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Xuancheng, then was recalled as Palace Secretary of the Secretariat, and left office on his mother’s death.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Xuancheng, then returned to the capital as Palace Secretary of the Secretariat, resigning when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he became Senior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, he was appointed Senior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 26 he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其秋，大舉北伐，淑侍坐從容曰：「今當鳴鑾中嶽，席捲趙、魏，檢玉岱宗，今其時也。

translations.literal: That autumn a great northern campaign was launched; Shu, attending at ease, said: “Now is the time to sound the imperial carriage at Mount Song, sweep through Zhao and Wei, and inspect the jade regalia at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the court launched a major northern expedition; Shu, seated in attendance, said calmly, “The moment has come to advance the imperial train to the central peak, roll up Zhao and Wei, and present the jade regalia at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 臣逢千載之會，願上《封禪書》一篇。

translations.literal: Your servant has met an age of a thousand years and wishes to present a memorial On the Feng and Shan Sacrifices.”
translations.idiomatic: I have been granted a once-in-a-millennium opportunity, and I wish to submit a treatise On the Feng and Shan Sacrifices.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「盛德之事，我何足以當之。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said: “Such an act of supreme virtue — how could I be worthy of it?”
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, “That is the work of the highest virtue — how could I presume to undertake it?”

sentences.zh: 」出為始興王征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Chief Administrator on the northern campaign staff of the Prince of Shixing, and Governor of Eastern Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Chief Administrator on the northern campaign staff of the Prince of Shixing and as Governor of Eastern Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 淑始到府，浚引見，謂曰：「不意舅遂垂屈佐。

translations.literal: When Shu first arrived at the princely headquarters, Jun received him and said: “I never expected that my uncle would stoop to serve as my aide.”
translations.idiomatic: When Shu first reached the prince’s headquarters, Jun summoned him and said, “I never thought my uncle would condescend to assist me.”

sentences.zh: 」淑答曰：「朝廷遣下官，本以光公府望。

translations.literal: Shu replied: “The court sent your humble servant here precisely to lend luster to the prince’s establishment.”
translations.idiomatic: Shu answered, “The court dispatched me here expressly to enhance the prestige of your highness’s command.”

sentences.zh: 」還為禦史中丞。

translations.literal: He was then recalled as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled to serve as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時索虜南侵，遂至瓜步，太祖使百官議防禦之術，淑上議曰：

translations.literal: At that time the northern barbarians invaded south as far as Guabu; the Emperor had the officials discuss measures of defense, and Shu submitted a proposal, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the northern forces pushed south as far as Guabu; the Emperor ordered the officials to debate defensive strategy, and Shu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞函車之獸，離山必斃；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that beasts that travel in covered wagons, once they leave the mountains, are sure to perish;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that beasts accustomed to riding in curtained carts will die once they leave the mountains;

sentences.zh: 絕波之鱗，宕流則枯。

translations.literal: fish that cross the waves, once cast into still backwaters, dry up.
translations.idiomatic: and fish that ride the billows wither when they are stranded in slack water.

sentences.zh: 羯寇遺醜，趨致畿甸，蟻萃螽集，聞已崩殪。

translations.literal: The remnant horde of the Jie raiders has rushed to reach the capital region; though they swarm like ants and locusts, word is that they are already collapsing and perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy’s surviving rabble has pressed toward the metropolitan districts; though they mass thick as ants and locusts, reports already say they are breaking up and dying off.

sentences.zh: 天險岩曠，地限深遐，故全魏戢其圖，盛晉輟其議，情屈力殫，氣挫勇竭，諒不虞於來臨，本無怵於能濟矣。

translations.literal: Heaven’s barriers are steep and vast, and the land’s limits are deep and remote; thus all Wei checked its designs and great Jin set aside its plans — their will bent and their strength spent, their spirit broken and their courage exhausted — surely they did not expect this advance, and never feared we could prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s ramparts are sheer and wide, and the earth’s bounds are deep and far; that is why Wei in its day restrained its ambitions and Jin in its glory stayed its plans — will broken, strength spent, courage drained — and they plainly did not foresee this invasion, nor ever believed we could overcome it.

sentences.zh: 乃者燮定攜遠，阻違授律，由將有弛拙，故士少鬥志。

translations.literal: Yet of late, in pacifying the distant tribes, orders were obstructed and discipline violated, because the generals grew lax and clumsy, so the soldiers lost heart for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently, while settling distant peoples, commands were blocked and military law ignored; commanders grew slack and inept, and the troops lost their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 圍潰之眾，匪寇傾淪，攻制之師，空自班散，濟西勁騎，急戰蹴旅，淮上訓卒，簡備靡旗。

translations.literal: The encircled masses did not fall because the enemy overthrew them; the attacking regiments dispersed of themselves; the crack cavalry west of the Ji fought in haste and trampled their own ranks; the trained soldiers on the Huai were picked over and lost their banners.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded bodies did not collapse because the foe overwhelmed them — the assault forces melted away on their own; the elite horsemen west of the Ji, fighting in haste, crushed their own columns; the drilled levies on the Huai were thinned out until their standards vanished.

sentences.zh: 是由綏整寡衷，戎昭多昧，遂使栲潞入患，泉伊來擾，紛殄姬風，泯毒禹績，騰書有渭陰之迫，懸烽均咸陽之警。

translations.literal: Hence lax discipline and little unity of purpose, and much obscurity in military glory, so that calamity entered through Gaolu and Lu, and raids came from Quan and Yi, defiling the legacy of the Zhou and poisoning the achievements of Yu; urgent dispatches spoke of peril west of the Wei, and beacon fires matched the alarms at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: This came of slack order and divided counsels, of clouded martial purpose, so that disaster entered from the Gaolu and Lu region and raids came from Quan and Yi, sullying the civilizing heritage of the Zhou and tainting the labors of Yu; urgent reports told of danger west of the Wei, and signal fires rivaled the warnings once raised at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 然而切揣虛實，伏匿先彰，校索伎能，譎詭既顯。

translations.literal: Yet close reckoning of fact and fiction shows that what was hidden has already been exposed; comparison of their skills and ours shows that their deceits are already plain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a careful weighing of truth and pretense shows their hidden weaknesses already revealed; a tally of their abilities against ours shows their stratagems already unmasked.

sentences.zh: 綿地千里，彌行阻深，表裏躓硋，後先介逼。

translations.literal: Though their territory spans a thousand li, every advance is blocked by depth; within and without they stumble, and front and rear press upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: Though their lands stretch a thousand li, each march meets deep obstruction; inwardly and outwardly they are checked, and those before and behind crowd one another.

sentences.zh: 舍陵衍之習，競湍沙之利。

translations.literal: They have abandoned their habit of campaigning over open hills and marshes, and vie for advantage on rushing sands.
translations.idiomatic: They have cast off their accustomed warfare over rolling hills and floodplains, and now compete for gain on treacherous shoals.

sentences.zh: 今虹見萍生，土膏泉動，津陸陷溢，痁禍洊興，芻稿已單，米粟莫系，水宇衿帶，進必傾殞，河隘扁固，退亦墮滅。

translations.literal: Now rainbows appear and duckweed sprouts; the soil is moist and springs stir; fords and roads sink and overflow; pestilence rises again and again; fodder is already spent and grain cannot be secured; the rivers and marshes girdle them like a collar — if they advance they must topple and perish; the river narrows and the banks are firm — if they retreat they likewise fall to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Now rainbows arc and duckweed spreads, the earth softens and springs quicken, crossings flood and roads give way, and sickness breaks out in waves; fodder is exhausted and grain cannot be gathered; rivers and wetlands clasp them like a noose — advance, and they are doomed to crash; the stream is narrow and the banks unyielding — retreat, and they are likewise destroyed.

sentences.zh: 所謂棲烏於烈火之上，養魚于叢棘之中。

translations.literal: This is what is called roosting birds upon blazing fire and raising fish amid thorn thickets.
translations.idiomatic: This is what people mean by perching birds on living flame and keeping fish in a bramble patch.

sentences.zh: 或謂損緩江右，寬繕淮內。

translations.literal: Some say we should reduce our hold on the lands right of the Yangzi and relax defenses within the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that we should loosen our grip on the territory south of the Yangzi and ease preparations within the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 竊謂拯扼閩城，舊史為允，棄遠涼士，前言稱非。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that to rescue and hold Min city accords with old histories, but to abandon distant Liang lands was condemned in earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: I maintain that to defend and hold Min city wins approval in the old histories, whereas to cast off distant Liang territory was judged wrong in earlier counsel.

sentences.zh: 限此要荒，猶弗委割。

translations.literal: Even at the limits of this frontier waste we still do not lightly yield a slice.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the edge of this remote frontier we still refuse to surrender an inch lightly.

sentences.zh: 況聯被京國，咫尺神甸，數州摧掃，列邑殲痍，山淵反覆，草木塗地。

translations.literal: How much less when the capital itself is linked in suffering, the sacred precincts only a few hundred paces away, several provinces swept bare, and town after town laid waste, until mountains and rivers are overturned and grass and trees cover the ground.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the capital itself is stricken, the imperial domain only a step away, whole provinces scoured clean, and city after city ruined, until hills and streams are overturned and the land is buried under grass and trees.

sentences.zh: 今丘賦千乘，井算萬集，肩摩倍于長安，締袂百於臨淄，什一而籍，實慊氓願，履畝以稅，既協農和。

translations.literal: Today the hill tax supplies a thousand chariots and the well tax gathers ten thousand households; shoulders crowd thicker than in Chang’an and linked sleeves outnumber those in Linzi; a one-in-ten levy truly satisfies the people’s wish, and taxation by the acre already harmonizes with the farmers’ peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the land tax can equip a thousand war-chariots and the household registers gather myriads of families; the crowds press shoulder to shoulder more densely than in Chang’an, and linked sleeves outnumber those of Linzi; a tithe in ten truly answers the people’s desire, and levies measured by the acre already accord with the farmers’ ease.

sentences.zh: 戶競戰心，人含銳志，皆欲贏糧請奮，釋緯乘城。

translations.literal: Households compete in warlike resolve and every man harbors a keen will; all wish to carry extra rations and beg to fight, to lay aside the loom and mount the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Every household burns with martial zeal and every man nurses a sharp purpose; all want to bring extra grain and volunteer for battle, to leave the loom and man the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 謂宜懸金鑄印，要壯果之士，重幣甘辭，招摧決之將，舉薦板築之下，抽登臺皁之間，賞之以焚書，報之以相爵，俄而昭才賀闕，異能間至。

translations.literal: It is fitting to hang out gold and cast seals, to summon bold and resolute men, to offer heavy gifts and gracious words, to recruit commanders ready to break the foe, to raise men from beneath the pounding-board and draw them from among the humble at court, rewarding them with the burning of records and repaying them with enfeoffment — and soon outstanding talent will fill the gates and uncommon ability will arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: We should post gold and cast seals, call for the brave and decisive, offer rich rewards and winning words, enlist generals eager to smash the enemy, promote men from the lowest labor and pull talent from the humblest ranks, pay them with the burning of past offenses and answer them with titles of nobility — and in no time gifted men will crowd the court and rare abilities will appear one after another.

sentences.zh: 戎貪而無謀，肆而不整，迷乎向背之次，謬於合散之宜，犯軍志之極害，觸兵家之甚諱。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians are greedy and without plan, reckless and undisciplined, confused about whom to face and whom to turn from, mistaken in when to unite and when to scatter, violating the gravest harm in military doctrine and touching the greatest taboo of the art of war.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is grasping yet unreflecting, wild yet disorderly, blind to the sequence of friend and foe, wrong in the timing of concentration and dispersion, running against the deadliest fault in military law and the deepest prohibition of strategists.

sentences.zh: 鹹畜憤矣，僉策戰矣，稱願影從，謠言緡命。

translations.literal: All store up anger, all plot for battle; they declare their wish to follow in our shadow, and rumor binds them to our command.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm has hoarded its wrath and every counsel turns to battle; men say they long to follow our lead, and popular report ties them to our orders.

sentences.zh: 宜選敢悍數千，騖行潛掩，偃旗裹甲，鉗馬銜枚，檜稽而起，晨壓未陣，旌噪亂舉，火鼓四臨，使景不暇移，塵不及起，無不禽鎩獸讋，冰解霧散，掃洗哨類，漂鹵浮山。

translations.literal: We should choose several thousand daring fighters, ride swiftly in secret encirclement, lower banners and wrap armor, muzzle horses and take gag-sticks in the mouth, rise from Guiji at dawn and press the enemy before their array is formed; when banners shout and confusion rises, with drums and fire on four sides, they will have no moment to shift position nor time to raise the dust — none will fail to be seized and shattered like beasts in terror, melting like ice and scattering like mist, sweeping away the outpost bands and floating their spoils like foam upon the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Select several thousand fierce troops, gallop in concealed envelopment, lower standards and bind on armor, bit the horses and forbid speech, rise from Guiji at dawn and press them before their formations stand; let banners roar and confusion break out, with drums and fire closing on every side, so they cannot shift ground or even lift dust — none will escape being seized and broken like panic-stricken beasts, dissolving like ice and mist, scouring the frontier bands and heaping their plunder like drift upon the hills.

sentences.zh: 如有決罦漏網，逡窠逗穴，命淮、汝戈船，遏其還徑，兗部勁卒，梗其歸塗。

translations.literal: If any escape the net through a gap in judgment, lingering in burrows and hiding in holes, then order the war-boats of the Huai and Ru to block their return, and the crack troops of Yan province to choke their homeward road.
translations.idiomatic: Should any slip through a breach in the net, lingering in dens and skulking in holes, set the war-junks of the Huai and Ru to cut off their retreat and the elite soldiers of Yan to bar their homeward path.

sentences.zh: 必剪元雄，懸首麾下，乃將只輪不反，戰轊無旋矣。

translations.literal: We are sure to cut down their chief leaders and hang their heads beneath our banners; then their chariots will return with but a single wheel, and their war-chariots will not come back.
translations.idiomatic: We shall surely cut down their chieftains and hang their heads before our standards; then their chariots will return with only one wheel, and their battle-cars will not wheel back at all.

sentences.zh: 於是信臣騰威，武士繕力，緹組接陰，鞞柝聯響。

translations.literal: Thereupon loyal ministers will display their authority and warriors will renew their strength; brocade cords will link the camps in shadow and watch-drums will sound in unbroken answer.
translations.idiomatic: Then faithful ministers will mount in majesty and fighting men will sharpen their strength; brocade lines will join camp to camp in shadow, and watch-drums will answer one another without cease.

sentences.zh: 若其偽遁羸張，出沒無際，楚言漢旆，顯默如神，固已日月蔽虧，川穀蕩貿。

translations.literal: If they feign retreat and feign weakness, appearing and vanishing without limit, with Chu speech and Han banners, showing themselves and hiding like spirits — then already sun and moon are dimmed and rivers and valleys overturned in trade.
translations.idiomatic: If they pretend flight and feign weakness, surfacing and disappearing without end, with the speech of Chu and the banners of Han, visible and hidden as if by divine art — then already sun and moon are eclipsed and streams and valleys are thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 負塞殘孽，阻山燼黨，收險竊命，憑城借土，則當因威席捲，乘機芟剿。

translations.literal: As for the remnant rebels holding the passes, the bandits burned out in the mountains who seize the defiles and steal their lives, relying on walled towns and borrowed soil — we should then ride our prestige in a sweeping advance and seize the moment to mow them down.
translations.idiomatic: As for the broken remnants blocking the passes, the mountain bands burned to ash who cling to narrow ground and steal a living, trusting to walled cities and stolen earth — we should then roll forward on our authority and, seizing the opportunity, cut them down.

sentences.zh: 泗、汴秀士，星流電燭，徐、阜嚴兵，雨湊雲集，蹶亂桑溪之北，搖潰浣海以南，絕其心根，勿使能植，銜索之枯，幾何不蠹。

translations.literal: The fine warriors of Si and Bian will stream like stars and flash like lightning; Xu and Fu will muster strict troops, gathering like rain and clouds—trampling disorder north of Sang Creek, rocking collapse south of Huan River—cutting off their heart-root so they cannot take hold again; withers bound by rope, how can they fail to rot?
translations.idiomatic: The fine warriors of Si and Bian will stream like stars and flash like lightning. Xu and Fu will muster strict troops, gathering like rain and clouds, trampling disorder north of Sang Creek and rocking collapse south of Huan River. Cut off their heart-root so they cannot take hold again. Withers bound by rope—how can they fail to rot?

sentences.zh: 是由涸澤而漁，焚林而狩，若浚風之亻舞輕籜，杲日之拂浮霜。

translations.literal: Thus is it like draining the marsh to fish and burning the forest to hunt—like a piercing wind shaking light bamboo sheaths, like bright sun brushing floating frost.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it will be like draining the marsh to fish and burning the forest to hunt, like a piercing wind shaking light bamboo sheaths, like bright sun brushing floating frost.

sentences.zh: 既而尉洽荷掠之餘，望吊網悲之鬼。

translations.literal: Then pacify those who remain from lotus-plunder, gaze in condolence upon ghosts netted in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Then pacify those who remain from lotus-plunder and gaze in condolence upon ghosts netted in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 然後天行樞運，猋舉煙升，青蓋西巡，翠華東幸，經啟州野，滌一軫策，俾高闕再勒，燕然後銘。

translations.literal: After that heaven moves the pivot of fate, tempest rises and smoke ascends—the blue canopy tours west, the emerald pennant journeys east—opening and cleansing the provinces and wilds, washing clean in one sweep of the whip—so that the high gate is inscribed again and Yanran marked afterward.
translations.idiomatic: After that heaven will move the pivot of fate, tempest will rise and smoke ascend. The blue canopy will tour west and the emerald pennant journey east, opening and cleansing the provinces and wilds and washing them clean in one sweep of the whip, so that the high gate is inscribed again and Yanran marked afterward.

sentences.zh: 方乃奠山沉河，創禮輯策，闡耀炎、昊之遺則，貫軼商、夏之舊文。

translations.literal: Only then sink offerings at the mountain and river, create rites and compile records, radiate the surviving rules of Yan and Hao, thread through and surpass the old texts of Shang and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Only then will you sink offerings at the mountain and river, create rites and compile records, radiate the surviving rules of Yan and Hao, and thread through and surpass the old texts of Shang and Xia.

sentences.zh: 今眾賈拳勇，而將術疏怯，意者稔泰日積，承平歲久，邑無驚赴之急，家緩饋戰之勤，闕閱訓之禮，簡參屬之飾，且亦薦采之法，庸未蔇歟。

translations.literal: Now the masses are valiant in fist and courage, yet generals are lax and timid in method—may it be that long peace has accumulated day by day, years of undisturbed rule prolonged; no town has the urgency of answering alarm bells, no household the diligence of supplying war; the rites of drill and inspection are wanting, the ornaments of review and assignment are scant—and perhaps the method of recommended selection is not yet thorough?
translations.idiomatic: Now the masses are valiant in fist and courage, yet generals are lax and timid in method. May it be that long peace has accumulated day by day and years of undisturbed rule have grown prolonged, so that no town feels the urgency of answering alarm bells and no household keeps the diligence of supplying war. The rites of drill and inspection are wanting, and the ornaments of review and assignment are scant. Perhaps the method of recommended selection is not yet thorough?

sentences.zh: 若乃邦造裏選，攉論深切，躬擐盡幽，斬帶尋遠，設有沉明能照，俊偉自宣，誠感泉雨，流通金石，氣懾飛、賁，知窮苴、起，審邪正順逆之數，達昏明益損之宜，能睽合民心，愚睿物性，登丹墀而敷策，躡青蒲而揚謀，上說辰鑒，下弭素言，足以安民紓國，救災恤患。

translations.literal: If within the state's crafting, in village selection, one plumbs discourse to the depth, personally tests the utmost hidden, cuts the sash to seek the far—suppose there is one with profound clarity that shines, commanding talent that declares itself, sincerity that moves spring rains and flows through metal and stone, spirit that awes Fei and Ben, knowing that reaches Ju and Qi, discerning the numbers of wrong and right, bent and straight, understanding the fitting of obscurity and brightness, loss and gain, able to harmonize the people's hearts and know dull and sharp natures of things—ascend the red terrace and spread strategies, tread green rush and raise counsel above, persuading the celestial mirror below quieting plain words—enough to settle the people and ease the state, rescue disaster and pity the afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: If, within the state's crafting and in village selection, one plumbs discourse to the depth, personally tests the utmost hidden, and cuts the sash to seek the far, suppose there is one whose profound clarity shines forth and whose commanding talent declares itself, whose sincerity moves spring rains and flows through metal and stone, whose spirit awes Fei and Ben, whose knowing reaches Ju and Qi, who discerns the numbers of wrong and right, bent and straight, who understands the fitting of obscurity and brightness, loss and gain, who can harmonize the people's hearts and know the dull and sharp natures of things, who ascends the red terrace and spreads strategies and treads green rush to raise counsel above, persuading the celestial mirror and below quieting plain words—such a one would be enough to settle the people and ease the state, rescue disaster and pity the afflicted.

sentences.zh: 則宜拔過寵貴之上，褒升戚舊之右，別其旂章，榮其班祿，出得專譽，使不稟命。

translations.literal: Then he should be pulled above favored nobility, honored and promoted above kin of merit—given his own banner and insignia, glory in his rank and salary; going forth he may claim sole authority, orders need not be received.
translations.idiomatic: Then he should be pulled above favored nobility and honored and promoted above kin of merit. Give him his own banner and insignia and glory in rank and salary. Let him go forth with sole authority, without needing to receive orders.

sentences.zh: 降席折節，同廣武之請；

translations.literal: Lower your mat and bend your joint, as at Guangwu's request;
translations.idiomatic: Lower your mat and bend your joint, as at Guangwu's request;

sentences.zh: 設壇致禮，均淮陰之授。

translations.literal: raise an altar and perform rites, equal to bestowing command at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: raise an altar and perform rites, equal to bestowing command at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 必有要盟之功，竊符之捷。

translations.literal: There will surely be the achievement of covenant oath, the success of stealing the tally.
translations.idiomatic: There will surely be the achievement of a covenant oath and the success of stealing the tally.

sentences.zh: 夷裔暴狠，內外侮棄，始附之眾，分茷無序，蠱以威利，勢必攜離，首順之徒，靡然自及。

translations.literal: The barbarian tribes are violent and cruel, deserted within and without; those first attached are divided and without order; inflamed by authority and profit, they are bound to split apart; those who led the way will of themselves reach you.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian tribes are violent and cruel and deserted within and without. Those first attached are divided and without order. Inflamed by authority and profit, they are bound to split apart, and those who led the way will of themselves come over to you.

sentences.zh: 今淶繹故典，瀍土纓緌，翦焉幽播，折首凶狡。

translations.literal: Now distill the old canons, rinse the soil and tether; shear and scatter the hidden, cut off the heads of the fierce and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Now distill the old canons, rinse the soil and tether, shear and scatter the hidden, and cut off the heads of the fierce and cunning.

sentences.zh: 是猶眇者願明，痿之思步，動商遄會，功終易感。

translations.literal: It is like the near-sighted longing for brightness, the lame longing to walk—when the merchant pitch sounds, achievement at last is easy to feel.
translations.idiomatic: It is like the near-sighted longing for brightness and the lame longing to walk: when the merchant pitch sounds, achievement at last is easy to feel.

sentences.zh: 劫晉在於善覘，全鄭實寄良諜，多縱反間，汨惑心耳，發險易之前，抵興喪之術，沖其猜伏，拂其嫌嗜，汨以連率之貴，餌以析壤之資。

translations.literal: Seizing Jin lay in keen observation; preserving Zheng truly rested on good spies—multiply wandering agents, muddy and confuse their hearts and ears; send before danger and easy, strike with arts of rise and fall; pierce their suspicions hidden, brush their dislikes cherished; muddy them with the honor of joint command, bait them with the asset of carved territory.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing Jin lay in keen observation, and preserving Zheng truly rested on good spies. Multiply wandering agents and muddy and confuse their hearts and ears. Send counsel before danger and ease, and strike with the arts of rise and fall. Pierce their hidden suspicions and brush their cherished dislikes. Muddy them with the honor of joint command and bait them with the asset of carved territory.

sentences.zh: 罄筆端之用，展辭鋒之銳，振辯則堅圍可解，馳羽而岩邑易傾。

translations.literal: Exhaust the uses of the brush tip, unfold the sharp edge of rhetoric—shake debate and solid walls can be opened, fly the letter and steep towns easily topple.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust the uses of the brush tip and unfold the sharp edge of rhetoric. Shake debate and solid walls can be opened; fly the letter and steep towns easily topple.

sentences.zh: 必府鬲土崩，枝幹瓦裂，故燕、樂相悔，項、範交疑矣。

translations.literal: Surely the granary-like storehouse will crumble within, branches and trunks split like tiles—thus Yan and Yue regretted each other, Xiang and Fan came to mutual doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the granary-like storehouse will crumble within and branches and trunks will split like tiles. Thus Yan and Yue regretted each other, and Xiang and Fan came to mutual doubt.

sentences.zh: 或乃言約功深，事邇應廣，齊圉反駕，趙養還君，盡輿誦之道，畢能事之效。

translations.literal: Or again words few yet achievement deep, matter near yet response wide—Qi lord turned the carriage, Zhao nursed and returned the lord—entirely the way of street recitation, fully the effect of exhausting ability.
translations.idiomatic: Or again, though words be few the achievement is deep, though the matter be near the response is wide: the lord of Qi turned his carriage, and Zhao nursed and returned its lord. Entirely this is the way of street recitation and fully the effect of exhausting ability.

sentences.zh: 臣幸得出內層禁，遊心明代，澤與身泰，恩隨年行，無以逢迎昌運，潤飾鴻法。

translations.literal: Your servant is fortunate to have come from the inner layered prohibitions and to roam the heart in a bright age—favor has kept pace with the body, grace has moved with the years; he has no means to meet and welcome an auspicious fortune, to moisten and adorn the grand law.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is fortunate to have come from the inner layered prohibitions and to roam the heart in a bright age. Favor has kept pace with my body and grace has moved with the years, yet I have no means to meet and welcome an auspicious fortune or to moisten and adorn the grand law.

sentences.zh: 今塗有遺鏃，蠆未息蜂，敢思涼識，少酬閎施。

translations.literal: Now on the road are arrows left behind, scorpions and bees not yet stilled—I venture to bring forth modest views and repay a little the broad bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Now on the road lie arrows left behind, and scorpions and bees are not yet stilled. I venture to bring forth modest views and repay a little the broad bestowal.

sentences.zh: 但坐幕既乏昭文，免胄不能致果，竊觀都護之邊論，屬國之兵謨，終、晁之抗辭，杜、耿之言事，咸云及經之棘，猶闕上算，燭郛之敬，裁收下策。

translations.literal: Yet sitting in the tent there is lack of Zhao Wen, removing helm cannot bring result—I have observed the border discourse of the Chief Protector, the military stratagems of the Court of Dependencies, the resisting words of Zhong and Chao, the policy speeches of Du and Geng—all say that reaching the thorn of the classics still lacks the upper calculation, and the respect of Zhu Fu barely adopts the lower stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sitting in the tent there is lack of Zhao Wen, and removing the helm cannot bring result. I have observed the border discourse of the Chief Protector, the military stratagems of the Court of Dependencies, the resisting words of Zhong and Chao, and the policy speeches of Du and Geng. All say that reaching the thorn of the classics still lacks the upper calculation, and the respect shown by Zhu Fu barely adopts the lower stratagem.

sentences.zh: 自恥懦木，智不綜微，敢露昧見，無會昭采。

translations.literal: I myself am ashamed at timid wood, wisdom not weaving the minute—I venture to disclose a dark view, without meeting bright selection.
translations.idiomatic: I myself am ashamed at timid wood and wisdom that does not weave the minute. I venture to disclose a dark view, without meeting bright selection.

sentences.zh: 淑喜為誇誕，每為時人所嘲。

translations.literal: Shu delighted in grand and extravagant discourse and was often mocked by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Shu delighted in grand and extravagant discourse and was often mocked by men of the time.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗送錢三萬餉淑，一宿複遣追取，謂使人謬誤，欲以戲淑。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shixing, Jun, once sent thirty thousand cash to supply Shu; after one night he again sent to recover it, saying the messenger had erred and intending to tease Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shixing, Jun, once sent thirty thousand cash to supply Shu. After one night he sent again to recover it, saying the messenger had erred and intending to tease Shu.

sentences.zh: 淑與浚書曰：「袁司直之視館，敢寓書于上國之宮尹。

translations.literal: Shu wrote to Jun: "Yuan, Director of the Secretariat, viewing the lodging-house, ventures to lodge a letter with the palace steward of the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote to Jun, "Yuan, Director of the Secretariat, viewing the lodging-house, ventures to lodge a letter with the palace steward of the upper state.

sentences.zh: 日者猥枉泉賦，降委弊邑。

translations.literal: Recently you wrongly sent a spring levy, lowering it upon our poor district.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you wrongly sent a spring levy, lowering it upon our poor district.

sentences.zh: 弊邑敬事是遑，無或違貳。

translations.literal: Our poor district respectfully attends to the matter and dares not be double-minded.
translations.idiomatic: Our poor district respectfully attends to the matter and dares not be double-minded.

sentences.zh: 懼非郊贈之禮，覲饗之資，不虞君王惠之於是也，是有懵焉。

translations.literal: We fear it is not the gift of suburban presentation or the resource for audience and feast; we did not expect the king's grace in this, and therefore there is confusion.
translations.idiomatic: We fear it is not the gift of suburban presentation or the resource for audience and feast. We did not expect the king's grace in this, and therefore there is confusion.

sentences.zh: 弗圖旦夕發咫尺之記，籍左右而請，以為胥授失旨，爰速先幣。

translations.literal: We did not imagine that within the space of a day and night a note of a foot's breadth would issue, and through your attendants a request would be made, thinking the grant had missed its intent and therefore hastening the first gift.
translations.idiomatic: We did not imagine that within the space of a day and night a note of a foot's breadth would issue, and through your attendants a request would be made, thinking the grant had missed its intent and therefore hastening the first gift.

sentences.zh: 曾是附庸臣委末學孤聞者，如之何勿疑。

translations.literal: For a dependent minister and one of slight learning and lonely hearing such as I, how could there be doubt?
translations.idiomatic: For a dependent minister and one of slight learning and lonely hearing such as I, how could there be doubt?

sentences.zh: 且亦聞之前志曰，七年之中，一與一奪，義士猶或非之。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard in former records that within seven years, one grant and one withdrawal—even a man of righteousness might find fault.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have heard in former records that within seven years, one grant and one withdrawal—even a man of righteousness might find fault.

sentences.zh: 況密邇旬次，何其裒益之亟也。

translations.literal: How much more when it is close within a ten-day span—how sudden the increase and decrease!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when it is close within a ten-day span—how sudden the increase and decrease!

sentences.zh: 藉恐二三諸侯，有以觀大國之政。

translations.literal: I fear that the two or three feudal lords may thereby observe the government of the great state.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that the two or three feudal lords may thereby observe the government of the great state.

sentences.zh: 是用敢布心腹。

translations.literal: Therefore I venture to lay bare my inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I venture to lay bare my inmost heart.

sentences.zh: 弊室弱生，砥節清廉，好是潔直，以不邪之故，而貧聞天下。

translations.literal: My poor house and weak life polish the node and are pure and clean; I love what is pure and straight and, because I am not crooked, my poverty is known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: My poor house and weak life polish the node and are pure and clean. I love what is pure and straight, and because I am not crooked my poverty is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 甯有昧夫嗟金者哉。

translations.literal: Could there be one blind who sighs over gold?
translations.idiomatic: Could there be one blind who sighs over gold?

sentences.zh: 不腆供賦，束馬先璧以俟命。

translations.literal: Unworthily I supply the levy, bind horses and first present disks and await command.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthily I supply the levy, bind horses and first present disks, and await command.

sentences.zh: 唯執事所以圖之。」

translations.literal: Only let the steward take thought for it."
translations.idiomatic: Only let the steward take thought for it."

sentences.zh: 遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 元兇將為弑逆，其夜淑在直，二更許，呼淑及蕭斌等流涕謂曰：「主上信讒，將見罪廢。

translations.literal: The arch-criminal was about to commit regicide; that night Shu was on night duty; at the second watch he summoned Shu and Xiao Bin and others, and with tears said: "The emperor trusts slander and is about to punish and depose me.
translations.idiomatic: The arch-criminal was about to commit regicide. That night Shu was on night duty. At the second watch he summoned Shu and Xiao Bin and others and, weeping, said, "The emperor trusts slander and is about to punish and depose me.

sentences.zh: 內省無過，不能受枉。

translations.literal: Looking within, I have no fault and cannot accept wrongful ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Looking within, I have no fault and cannot accept wrongful ruin.

sentences.zh: 明旦便當行大事，望相與戮力。

translations.literal: Tomorrow morning I shall at once carry out the great affair; I hope you will join your strength with mine.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow morning I shall at once carry out the great affair. I hope you will join your strength with mine.

sentences.zh: 」淑及斌並曰：「自古無此，願加善思。

translations.literal: " Shu and Bin both said: "From antiquity there has never been this; I beg you to think more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu and Bin both said, "From antiquity there has never been this. I beg you to think more carefully.

sentences.zh: 」劭怒變色，左右皆動。

translations.literal: " Shao grew angry and changed color, and those at his side all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao grew angry and changed color, and those at his side all stirred.

sentences.zh: 斌懼，乃曰：「臣昔忝伏事，常思效節，況憂迫如此，輒當竭身奉令。

translations.literal: Bin was afraid and then said: "Your servant formerly served at your side and often thought to repay you with loyal effort; now that distress presses so close, I shall at once exhaust body and obey command.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was afraid and then said, "Your servant formerly served at your side and often thought to repay you with loyal effort. Now that distress presses so close, I shall at once exhaust my body and obey your command.

sentences.zh: 」淑叱之曰：「卿便謂殿下真有是邪？

translations.literal: " Shu rebuked him and said: "Do you then suppose His Highness truly means this?
translations.idiomatic: " Shu rebuked him and said, "Do you then suppose His Highness truly means this?

sentences.zh: 殿下幼時嘗患風，或是疾動耳。

translations.literal: His Highness in youth once suffered from wind; perhaps this is only the illness stirring.
translations.idiomatic: His Highness in youth once suffered from wind. Perhaps this is only the illness stirring.

sentences.zh: 」劭愈怒，因問曰：「事當克不？

translations.literal: " Shao grew still angrier and therefore asked: "Will the affair succeed or not?
translations.idiomatic: " Shao grew still angrier and therefore asked, "Will the affair succeed or not?

sentences.zh: 」淑曰：「居不疑之地，何患不克。

translations.literal: " Shu said: "Occupying a position free from doubt, what worry is there that it will not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: " Shu said, "Occupying a position free from doubt, what worry is there that it will not succeed?

sentences.zh: 但既克之後，為天地之所不容，大禍亦旋至耳。

translations.literal: But once it has succeeded, you will not be tolerated by heaven and earth, and great calamity will swiftly arrive.
translations.idiomatic: But once it has succeeded, you will not be tolerated by heaven and earth, and great calamity will swiftly arrive.

sentences.zh: 願急息之。

translations.literal: I wish you would stop it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to stop it at once.

sentences.zh: 」劭左右引淑等袴褶，又就主衣取錦，截三尺為一段，又中破，分斌、淑及左右，使以縛袴。

translations.literal: " Shao's attendants pulled Shu and the others by their kuzhe; they also went to the master of robes to get brocade, cut three-chi sections, split them down the middle, divided them among Bin, Shu, and those at the side, and had them use the pieces to bind their trousers.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao's attendants seized Shu and the others by their kuzhe. They also took brocade from the master of robes, cut it into three-chi lengths, split each length down the middle, and gave pieces to Bin, Shu, and the attendants to bind up their trousers.

sentences.zh: 淑出環省，繞床行，至四更乃寢。

translations.literal: Shu left the duty quarters, walked around his bed, and only at the fourth watch did he sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Shu returned to his quarters, paced around his bed, and did not sleep until the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 劭將出，已與蕭斌同載，呼淑甚急，淑眠終不起。

translations.literal: Shao was about to depart, already sharing a carriage with Xiao Bin; he called urgently for Shu, but Shu slept and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was about to set out, already in the same carriage as Xiao Bin. He called urgently for Shu, but Shu slept on and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 劭停車奉化門，催之相續。

translations.literal: Shao halted the carriage at Fenghua Gate, urgings following one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Shao stopped the carriage at Fenghua Gate, and the summons came in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 徐起至車後，劭使登車，又辭不上。

translations.literal: Shu slowly rose and went behind the carriage; Shao ordered him to mount, but he again declined and would not get on.
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose slowly and went to the rear of the carriage. Shao ordered him to mount, but he again refused and would not board.

sentences.zh: 劭因命左右：「與手刃。

translations.literal: Shao therefore ordered those at his side: "Kill him with your own blades.
translations.idiomatic: Shao therefore ordered those at his side, "Kill him with your own blades.

sentences.zh: 」見殺於奉化門外，時年四十六。

translations.literal: " He was killed outside Fenghua Gate, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: " He was killed outside Fenghua Gate, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 劭即位，追贈太常，賜賵甚厚。

translations.literal: When Shao took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Minister of Ceremonies and granted funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Shu as Grand Minister of Ceremonies and granted very generous funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子幾、敳、棱、凝、標。

translations.literal: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.

sentences.zh: 敳，世祖步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Ai was Footsoldier Commandant under Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Ai served as Footsoldier Commandant under Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 凝，太宗世禦史中丞，出為晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Ning was Censor-in-Chief in Taizong's reign and went out as Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was Censor-in-Chief under Emperor Taizong and later went out as Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太宗初與四方同反，兵敗歸降，以補劉湛冠軍府主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's reign he rebelled together with the four directions, was defeated and surrendered, and was made to fill the post of Registrar in Liu Zhan's Champion General's office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taizong's reign he joined the rebellion on all sides, was defeated and surrendered, and was appointed Registrar in Liu Zhan's Champion General's office.

sentences.zh: 淑諸子並早卒。

translations.literal: All of Shu's sons died young.
translations.idiomatic: All of Shu's sons died young.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天長地久，人道則異於斯。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Heaven is long and earth enduring, but the human way differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Heaven is long and earth enduring, but the human way is not like this.

sentences.zh: 蕣華朝露，未足以言也。

translations.literal: Hibiscus flower and morning dew are not enough to express it.
translations.idiomatic: Daylily bloom and morning dew scarcely suffice to describe it.

sentences.zh: 其間夭遽，曾何足雲。

translations.literal: Those who die young in between—what is there worth saying?
translations.idiomatic: Those cut off in their prime—what is there worth saying?

sentences.zh: 宜任心去留，不以存沒嬰心。

translations.literal: One ought to let the heart go or stay as it will and not let existence or extinction trouble the mind.
translations.idiomatic: The heart should be free to come or go, and not be bound by life or death.

sentences.zh: 徒以靈化悠遠，生不再來，雖天行路險，而未之斯遇，謂七尺常存，百年可保也。

translations.literal: Only because spiritual transformation is distant and life does not return—though heaven's path is perilous and one has not yet met with this—one thinks the seven-foot body will always remain and a hundred years can be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the spirit's changes lie far off and life does not return—though heaven's road is perilous and one has not yet met this fate—one supposes the body will always endure and a full lifetime can be kept.

sentences.zh: 所以據洪圖而輕天下，吝寸陰而敗尺璧。

translations.literal: Therefore one holds great designs and treats the realm lightly, begrudges every inch of shade and wastes the foot-measure jade.
translations.idiomatic: Hence men seize great designs and treat the realm lightly, begrudge every inch of time, and ruin the foot-long jade.

sentences.zh: 若乃義重乎生，空炳前誥，投軀殉主，世罕其人。

translations.literal: As for when righteousness outweighs life, brilliantly displayed in former edicts—casting one's body to die for one's lord: the age rarely has such men.
translations.idiomatic: When righteousness outweighs life, as former edicts brightly proclaim—giving one's body to die for one's lord—the age rarely produces such men.

sentences.zh: 若無陽源之節，丹青何貴焉爾！

translations.literal: Without Yangyuan's integrity, of what value would the annals be!
translations.idiomatic: Without Yangyuan's integrity, what would make the annals precious!
